messages:
alex: Heads up — ran a regional perf sweep for Llama2-70B, Mistral-7B, and Qwen-70B (AWQ4) across H100/A800/L40S. Seeing a consistent p99 spike in eu-west A800 nodes vs us-west H100s.

samir: Ok can you paste the exact config? p50/p99 numbers and seq length? :thinking:

alex: Test command:```python run_bench.py --model qwen-70b-awq --quant awq-4 --seq 4096 --batch 4 --warmup 50 --iters 200 --kernels auto```
Outputs (sample):
- us-west1 H100: p50=42ms p95=66ms p99=98ms tps=18
- eu-west1 A800: p50=55ms p95=120ms p99=230ms tps=9

maria: That's a huge delta on p99. Did kernel selection fall back on eu-west A800? Could be cutlass vs triton/flash-attn mismatch.

kevin: I pulled the logs — on A800 the runtime selected the "generic_attn" path for Qwen AWQ kernels due to an alignment check fail. That triggers slower memory copies and loses kv-cache coalescing.

alex: Repro: when I force kernel=flash_attn on A800 the job fails with OOM for 4096 seq; forced cutlass reduces p99 to ~140ms but still worse than H100.

samir: Is this only Qwen-AWQ or also Llama/Mistral?

alex: All three show differences but Qwen-AWQ is worst. Llama2 FP16 is relatively stable across regions (p99 ~110ms on A800), Mistral-7B has ~20% throughput drop on A800 vs H100.

maria: Could be multiple factors: kernel implementation (cutlass tuning), GPU SM versions, PCIe/NVLink config in region, and driver/cuda versions. Any driver diffs?

kevin: eu-west infra is on CUDA 12.2 + driver 535, us-west H100s are on 12.6 + 542. There's also a firmware mismatch on a rack with older sm-clocks. Opened infra ticket.

alex: Also saw KV-sharding differences: our routing put some requests on 2-GPU jobs in eu-west to meet capacity and we saw cross-GPU KV-sync overhead. H100 run was single-GPU per request.

bench-bot: perf-alert: qwen-70b-awq | eu-west1 A800 | p99 increase +135% vs baseline (us-west1 H100) | job: 1780005432-01

maria: For next step: 1) pin cuda/driver on eu-west to match us-west, 2) force single-GPU runs to isolate KV sync, 3) run kernel debug with env REDWOOD_DEBUG_KERNEL_SELECTION=1 and capture fallback reasons.

alex: I'll run steps 1-2 now and post results. Also want to test seq=8192 to exercise ROPE/GQA behavior — maybe kernel chooses different code path for long context.

samir: FYI, Qwen's ROPE implementation in our conversion had a small stride mismatch that makes some kernels opt-out for >4096. That explains fallback at 4096/8192. I pushed a fix to conversion branch; can try a rebuild with corrected stride. :eyes:

kevin: If rebuild isn't trivial, as a temporary measure we can add a region routing policy: prefer H100 for AWQ-quantized Qwen or fall back to FP16 variants on A800 to avoid p99 pain. That will affect capacity sizing though.

maria: Also run with bitsandbytes vs awq backends — we saw different memory layouts that alter kernel selection. Add --quant-backend=awq,bnb to sweep.

alex: Quick update after pinning driver + single-GPU: p99 on eu-west1 A800 dropped from 230ms -> 150ms for seq=4096, throughput still 11 tps. So driver mismatch explained part of it.

samir: Nice. Can you run the conversion-fixed build for stride mismatch and retest?

alex: Kicked off conversion build with corrected ROPE stride; bench queued. If that reduces fallback we should get closer to H100 numbers.

maria: Long term notes for the runbook: - prefer flash_attn path on H100 - add kernel selection telemetry (reason codes) - routing policy for quantized workloads by model+backend+region - include KV-shard penalty in capacity estimator

kevin: Agreed. For capacity sizing: assume a 1.8x p99 uplift for quantized Qwen on A800 unless kernel parity confirmed. Update capacity model and add cost delta to SRE dashboard.

alex: I'll post full log + perf csv when conversion build finishes. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
